name: NAVIGATOR HOLDINGS

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: Refusing on evidence is too convenient when the model actually runs. The base of $215.7 million is the mean of [$116.6M, $210.5M, $174.1M] — all of which PREDATE the record year — so the window excludes 2026 entirely and the base understates current generation rather than overstating it. That is the one direction of error that makes a refusal expensive: a genuinely cheap name is being declined because the analyst could not open a PDF.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: The 2026 interim cash-flow statement and the newbuild capital-expenditure schedule — how much of the record earnings converts to cash, and how much of that cash is already committed to the six vessels.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Only in summary, and what is visible cuts against the counter more than for it. Management's own guidance is that the third quarter moderates; the driver of the record quarter was a geopolitical disruption that has since reversed; and $336 million of obligations fall due within twelve months on a $1.5 billion market capitalisation, which is where the cash the counter wants to capitalise is going. The counter's factual premise is correct — the base does exclude the peak — but its conclusion does not follow, because what a shipping company earns at the top of a rate cycle is the least extrapolable number it produces.
devils_advocate.unresolved: Whether free cash flow after the newbuild programme is positive through 2027. That is the whole question and I could not read the document that answers it. The refusal is a statement about my evidence, not a claim that Navigator is expensive.

what_changed: The rate environment, in both directions, and none of it is in the model's window. The record Q2 came from geopolitical disruption to gas trade routes; that premium has since unwound with the agreement ending the US-Iran conflict and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, which appears in this brief's own Energy sector feed. Management explicitly expects third-quarter performance to MODERATE from the record second quarter as terminal volumes, utilisation and time-charter-equivalent rates ease. Separately the company secured financing for six newbuild vessels — four ethylene carriers delivering between December 2026 and December 2027 — and reports $1.389 billion of future obligations including debt, vessels under construction and leases, of which $336 million falls due within twelve months against a $1.5 billion market capitalisation. An activist position was reported on 2026-08-07.
consensus_case: Navigator owns the largest handysize liquefied-gas fleet and a half-share of the Morgan's Point ethylene export terminal, and 2026 has been the best year in its history. Second-quarter net income was $53.0 million, or $0.86 a share — the highest Navigator has ever reported — on record average charter rates, a time-charter equivalent of $33,946 a day, 90.8% utilisation and record terminal throughput of 374,278 tons as Europe and Asia pulled US ethylene. The dividend was raised to $0.08. The order book for handysize gas carriers is thin and US natural-gas-liquids production keeps growing, so the structural case is real. The shares are up 53% over twelve months and 17.7% over the last month, and at 1.5 billion dollars of market capitalisation the market is paying for a franchise, not for the 2026 rate environment to persist.
base_case_rationale: No base case is offered, and the reason is evidentiary rather than analytical. I could not read a single primary document for this company. Navigator is a foreign private issuer that reports on Form 20-F with interim results on Form 6-K; the engine indexes NO filings for it at all — the brief's 'Recent filings' section is empty and its 8-K exhibit list is empty — and an adhoc-fetch dispatch returned ZERO documents, exactly as it did for MRX on 2026-09-17. I therefore have no balance sheet, no cash-flow statement and no capital-expenditure schedule that I have personally checked, on a name carrying a +283% gap at the 98th percentile of its cohort. The standing rule is that an extreme gap is a suspected data error until the inputs are personally verified, and I verified none of them.
key_risks: Beta 0.47 with R-squared 0.078 gives a 7.3% WACC to a cyclical gas-shipping company — the documented low-fit beta bias that took all three Energy opportunistic slots on 2026-09-03; at a defensible shipping beta near 1.0-1.2 the WACC is roughly 9%, at which the market implies about -8% rather than -13.7%
The +283.4% gap comes from a +12.0% revenue-CAGR baseline measured from a weak 2021 through an all-time-record 2026 — a cycle artifact, not a growth rate
The engine indexes NO filings for this issuer, so the item 2.01/1.01/3.02 check that catches acquisitions and financings is structurally blind on every foreign private issuer in this universe
$1.389bn of future obligations including vessels under construction sit outside the enterprise value the model uses; $336m is due within twelve months
The brief dates the balance sheet 2026-06-30 and attributes it to a '20-F', which is an annual form for a December year-end filer — the provenance of the balance sheet is itself unclear
watch_for: Q3 2026 results, the first read on how far rates moderate from the record quarter
The newbuild delivery and payment schedule for the four ethylene carriers arriving December 2026 to December 2027
Whether the activist position reported on 2026-08-07 produces a capital-allocation change
Any route that makes 6-K interims reachable — that single change would make this name modellable
